replication.target_description: EmpaToM empathy: age group × emotionality interaction on valence ratings; independent younger/older MRI sample, after empathy-specific outlier exclusions.

n.location: Methods, Participants and Data analysis; Results §3.1
n.quote: The final sample comprised 42 younger (21 females, age range = 18–30, M = 24.00, s.d. = 3.20) and 44 older (22 females, age range = 65–77, M = 69.50, s.d. = 3.74) individuals. Furthermore, we excluded three participants (OA = 1, YA = 2) from the analysis of empathy
n.sample_role: participants in the target test; younger and older adult groups
n.exclusions: 15 of 101 excluded: inability to undergo scanning (5), hearing/sight problems (4), termination/technical problems (2), neurological abnormalities (4). Two below-chance participants retained. Button-box and sleep trials excluded and scores proportionally adjusted. Empathy additionally excludes 1 older and 2 younger extreme outliers (>3 s.d.); analytic 83 established from final 86 minus 3, consistent with F denominator df 81.

reported_success.quote: We were able to replicate the effect of age on empathy and compassion reported by Reiter et al. [62]

notes: Selected age × emotionality interaction: both papers explicitly identify this as the test for age differences in empathy. Other main effects are not substituted. Replication analytic n established by documented exclusions, not printed as a standalone total. Original bound on partial eta-squared preserved; no metric conversion.
